Pool query template results across servers

Source: R/queries.R
ds.omop.query.pool.Rd

Takes per-server results from ds.omop.query.exec and delegates to the exact server-owned pooling contract carried by that result. It never infers keys, count fields, rates, or statistics from column names.

Usage

ds.omop.query.pool(
  results,
  query_id = NULL,
  sensitive_fields = NULL,
  pool_strategy = "sum",
  policy = "strict",
  symbol = "omop",
  pooling_policy = NULL
)

Arguments

results

Named list of per-server data frames, as returned by ds.omop.query.exec.

query_id

Optional character query ID; when supplied, it must match the analysis identity carried by results.

sensitive_fields

Deprecated and unsupported; must remain NULL.

pool_strategy

Deprecated and unsupported; must remain "sum".

policy

Deprecated alias of pooling_policy.

symbol

Character; the session symbol used when the OMOP connection was initialised (default: "omop").

pooling_policy

Character; suppression propagation policy. "strict" (the default) sets the pooled value to NA if any server suppressed the cell. "pooled_only_ok" sums only the non-suppressed values. See dsomop_conventions.

Value

A data frame with contractually pooled results, or NULL when the contracted estimand has no combinable result.

Details

Suppression-safe pooling policy: if any server suppressed a cell (marked as NA by the server's disclosure controls), the corresponding pooled cell also becomes NA under "strict" policy. This prevents reconstructing small-site counts by subtracting the pooled total from known large sites.

Deprecated

New code should use ds.omop.analysis.run, whose pooled element already contains the cross-server aggregation. This helper remains only as a contractual bridge for results from deprecated ds.omop.query.exec.

See also

ds.omop.analysis.run

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
results <- ds.omop.query.exec("condition_prevalence")
pooled <- ds.omop.query.pool(results, query_id = "condition_prevalence")
pooled
} # }
